entryPoint: SLA::priorityEscalation() in include/class.sla.php (lines 117-119) — a public, zero-argument instance method on the SLA ORM model (VerySimpleModel). It is the facade surface callers use to ask whether priority escalation is enabled for this SLA plan.
coreLogic: The entire method body is one inline expression: `return $this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE;`. `$this->flags` is the SLA's persisted bitmask column (ost_sla.flags), already loaded by the ORM when the row was fetched — no lazy load, no extra query. `FLAG_ESCALATE` = 0x0002 (class.sla.php line 28), one of four bit constants on SLA (FLAG_ACTIVE=0x0001, FLAG_ESCALATE=0x0002, FLAG_NOALERTS=0x0004, FLAG_TRANSIENT=0x0008). CRITICAL QUIRK TO PRESERVE: this line uses PHP's logical `&&` operator, NOT the bitwise `&` operator used everywhere else in this class for flag checks (isActive(): `$this->flags & self::FLAG_ACTIVE`; sendAlerts(): `0 === ($this->flags & self::FLAG_NOALERTS)`; getInfo(): `$this->flags & self::FLAG_ESCALATE`). Because `&&` always yields a strict bool in PHP and FLAG_ESCALATE (2) is itself always truthy, this expression is equivalent to `(bool)$this->flags` — it returns true whenever ANY flag bit is set (even if the FLAG_ESCALATE bit specifically is NOT set, e.g. flags=1/FLAG_ACTIVE only) and false only when flags is exactly 0. This is a pre-existing discrepancy versus the bitwise checks elsewhere in the class, but it is the current, real return contract and must be lifted verbatim — not 'corrected' to bitwise AND. Two related methods expose/persist the same bit but are OUT OF SCOPE for this seam: getInfo() (line 78) computes `$base['enable_priority_escalation'] = $this->flags & self::FLAG_ESCALATE;` (int 0 or 2, via correct bitwise AND) for staff-UI consumption; update($vars, &$errors) (lines 189-193) persists the bit back via `$this->flags = (...) | ($vars['enable_priority_escalation']) | (...)`, relying on the caller having already normalized $vars['enable_priority_escalation'] to 0 or FLAG_ESCALATE (2). Neither getInfo() nor update() calls priorityEscalation(), and priorityEscalation() calls neither of them — all three are independent readers/writers of the same $this->flags bit and must not be merged or cross-delegated.

It is currently dead/unused code: no controller, template, cron job (include/class.cron.php), or plugin invokes it.

orchestrator/agents/extractor.ts contains a documentation-only reference to `$sla->priorityEscalation()` inside its anti-recursion prompt text (an example of what the extracted service must NOT call back into) — this is pipeline tooling guidance, not an application call site.
inputShape: None. priorityEscalation() takes zero parameters; it operates entirely on the implicit $this SLA instance's already-loaded `flags` property (int, ORM column ost_sla.flags).
outputShape: bool (strict — PHP's `&&` operator always returns true/false regardless of operand types). Truthy: true whenever $this->flags is non-zero, i.e. any bit is set — not necessarily the FLAG_ESCALATE bit specifically (see the logical-AND quirk in coreLogic). Falsy: false only when $this->flags === 0. No mutation of $this or any argument; no new object allocated; nothing passed or returned by reference.
sideEffects: None beyond an in-memory property read: reads only $this->flags, already loaded by the ORM when the SLA row was fetched — no additional DB query, no lazy-load trigger.
No global state is read ($cfg or otherwise is not touched by this method).
No writes of any kind: no DB write, no cache write, no file I/O, no Signal::send.

getInfo() and update() (the two related flag accessors documented above) are NOT invoked by priorityEscalation() and must not be pulled into the extracted service — they are facade-level concerns out of scope for this seam.
constraints: Preserve the exact operator `$this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE` (logical AND) verbatim — do NOT rewrite it as `$this->flags & self::FLAG_ESCALATE` (bitwise AND) even though that matches the bitwise pattern used elsewhere in the class (getInfo(), isActive(), sendAlerts()). This is a real, pre-existing discrepancy that must be reproduced exactly, not fixed.
Return type must remain PHP bool for every input (guaranteed already since `&&` always yields bool).
flags=0 edge case: must return false (0 && 2 evaluates to false) — the one case where the logical-AND behavior happens to agree with bitwise intent.

flags set to any non-zero value that does NOT include the FLAG_ESCALATE bit (e.g. flags=1 / FLAG_ACTIVE only) must still return true under the current logical-AND behavior — this divergence from the 'escalation bit specifically' intent must be reproduced exactly, not corrected.
Method must keep its exact signature `function priorityEscalation()` (no parameters, public visibility) on the SLA facade after the strangler patch.
Reference the SLA::FLAG_ESCALATE constant (not the literal 2) from wherever the logic ends up, so the bit value stays single-sourced.

The extracted service must never call back into SLA::priorityEscalation() (anti-recursion) and must not reach into SLA::getInfo() or SLA::update() either, since those are separate facade-level accessors for the same bit and are out of scope for this seam.
No new DB reads/writes, global reads, or side effects may be introduced — the original method has none, so the extracted service must also have none.
harnessInputShape: JSON object with a single field: flags (integer) — the raw SLA.flags bitmask value used to construct an in-memory SLA instance (no DB write), then call priorityEscalation() on it and capture the boolean result. Use flags=2 (FLAG_ESCALATE bit only) for escalation enabled; flags=1 (FLAG_ACTIVE only, FLAG_ESCALATE bit unset) for escalation disabled — this is also the case that most clearly exposes the logical-AND quirk, since the current code still returns true here; and flags=0 for the flags=0 edge case, where both the actual logical-AND behavior and the 'intended' bitwise behavior agree on false.
